Executive Director

The Agency The Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC) is the largest municipal preservation agency in the nation. It is responsible for protecting New York City's architecturally, historically, and culturally significant buildings and sites by granting them landmark or historic district status and regulating them after designation. The agency is comprised of a panel of 11 commissioners who are appointed by the Mayor, and supported by a staff of approximately 80 preservationists, researchers, architects, historians, attorneys, archaeologists, and administrative employees. There are more than 38,500 designated buildings and sites in New York City, most of which are located in 159 historic districts across all five boroughs. Working at the Landmarks Preservation Commission provides a unique opportunity to develop professionally, engage with some of New York City’s most significant historic resources, serve the public, and help advance LPC’s mission to preserve and protect the city’s architectural, historical, and cultural heritage. The Team The Executive Director oversees the day-to-day administration of the agency, works closely with the Chair to set and carry out agency priorities, and oversees the agency’s regulatory, designation, strategic planning, and public affairs activities. Your Impact The Executive Director will have oversight of LPC’s $8.1 million budget and 80 employees and will develop and implement strategies to improve the agency’s performance. Working closely with the Chair, the Executive Director will develop agency-wide strategic plans, develop and advance policies, initiate and coordinate special projects, typically multi-department or multi-agency in nature. With the Chair, the Executive Director will oversee the work of the preservation, research, technology, external affairs, and administration departments. The Executive Director will ¿ Oversee agency operations, budget management, and human resources in coordination with the Chair and senior leadership team. ¿ Working with senior staff, plan and execute strategic initiatives to advance the agency’s mission and key priorities related to landmark designation and the agency’s regulatory work. Serve as a liaison to the Deputy Mayor of Housing and Planning's Office, work with city agencies on interagency initiatives, and engage with elected officials and the preservation and community stakeholders. ¿ Working with the public affairs team, oversee the agency's outreach, programming, and stakeholder communications. ¿ Represent the Commission at various public hearings, community board meetings, and professional forums. Minimum Qualification Requirements 1. A Master’s Degree in historic preservation, urban planning, architecture, public administration, or a related field, and five years of full-time experience working in the field of historic preservation, non-profit or government management, or a similar field; or 2. A Bachelor's Degree with specialization in one of the fields listed above, and ten years of full-time related experience; or 3. Education and/or experience equivalent to 1 & 2 above. Preferred Skills The ideal candidate would have: ¿ Demonstrated experience managing a large, complex organization or government agency. ¿ Proven track record of building and leading high-performing, diverse teams. ¿ A minimum of 8–10 years of progressively responsible experience in historic preservation, urban planning, public administration, or a related field. ¿ Deep knowledge in the field of historic preservation, and ideally, LPC’s policies and practices specifically. ¿ Experience working in government and an interest in working across multiple agencies and disciplines, and knowledge of New York City’s government and stakeholder community. ¿ Very strong written and oral communication skills, including experience with public presentations. ¿ Knowledge of New York City’s architecture, history, and development. How to Apply Please submit resume and cover letter to: JobsNYC at https://cityjobs.nyc.gov/ Please Note • The Landmarks Preservation Commission will only respond to qualified candidates. While we appreciate every applicant's interest, only those under consideration will be contacted. • If you were educated in a foreign school, you must be able to submit an evaluation of your foreign education from an approved organization. • Final appointment is subject to approval by the Office of Management and Budget. Circular Economy Program Manager

The NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) enriches the environment and protects public health for all New Yorkers by providing 1.1 billion gallons of high-quality drinking water, managing wastewater and stormwater, and reducing air, noise, and hazardous materials pollution. DEP is the largest combined municipal water and wastewater utility in the country, with nearly 6,000 employees. DEP's water supply system is comprised of 19 reservoirs and 3 controlled lakes throughout the system’s 2,000 square mile watershed that extends 125 miles north and west of the City. The Office of Energy and Resource Recovery Programs (Energy Office) is charged with plotting the course for DEP to meet its energy and carbon neutrality goals, as well as maximizing resource recovery. The Energy Office also provides energy and performance tracking, program assessment, scientific research, emergency planning and internal auditing services to DEP's operating bureaus. The Circular Economy Program Manager will provide technical and project management support to facility staff on Energy Office initiatives, including but not limited to: Biogas-to-Grid, Co-digestion, biogas beneficial use, and sewer and effluent heat recovery. The role will also focus on developing a pipeline of projects aimed at maximizing resource recovery and advancing the principles of a circular economy. Specific responsibilities will include: • Manage ongoing energy projects by coordinating with DEP operating bureaus, other City agencies, and contractors; overseeing design reviews, site visits, and approval processes; and supporting senior leadership with technical and operational input for decision-making. • Translate project concepts from ideation to execution by developing partnership models, contractual terms, and revenue-sharing arrangements, and by coordinating with stakeholders to ensure timely deployment. Track and report on project progress internally and with stakeholder bureaus. • Support and advise the Bureau throughout procurement, design, and policy-setting to influence decision-making processes toward energy and resource efficiency. Share energy and resource recovery best practices. Identify employee candidates for energy and resource recovery training. • Identify energy conservation opportunities and potential energy efficiency projects associated with wastewater conveyance, treatment processes, building systems, and other equipment. Contribute to project scopes of work and cost estimates. Support measurement and verification efforts. • Provide project management assistance, including developing and maintaining project plans and other documents, managing and coordinating project elements, reviewing milestones, and ensuring efficient progress on implementation through consistent monitoring of progress of initiatives and commitments. • Track and provide energy and resource recovery data needed for decision making, reporting and compliance purposes. Prepare, edit, proofread, and present high-quality reports, presentations, articles, meetings, correspondence, documents, reports and other energy and resource recovery communication materials and datasets.

1) A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university in architecture or architectural technology; biology; building science; chemistry; construction management; energy management; engineering or engineering technology; environmental science; facilities management; physics; or a related field, and four (4) years of satisfactory, full-time experience in energy generation or conservation work such as planning, developing, implementing, inspecting, analyzing, testing, and verifying interventions at facilities to generate clean energy or reduce energy usage, one (1) year of which must have been in an administrative, managerial, or executive capacity; or 2) An associate degree or sixty (60) semester credits in any of the disciplines described in “1” above from an accredited college or university, and six (6) years of satisfactory full-time experience as described in “1” above including one (1) year in an administrative, managerial, or executive capacity; or 3) A four (4) year high school diploma or its educational equivalent and eight (8) years of experience as described in “1” above, including one (1) year in an administrative, managerial, or executive capacity. 4) Education and experience which is equivalent to "1," "2," or "3" above. However, all candidates must have one (1) year of experience in an administrative, managerial, or executive capacity as described in “1” above. Education and experience will be credited as follows: a) One (1) year of experience, up to a maximum of four (4) years, will be credited for each year of experience in one or more of the following: i) Journey-level experience in one or more of the skilled building trades; or ii) Full-time experience in the construction, repair, alteration, and/or rehabilitation of buildings in the capacity of general contractor, superintendent of construction, procurement specialist, or, evaluator responsible for cost estimation; or iii) Full-time building construction management experience; or iv) Full-time experience in construction field supervision or inspection. b) Education will be credited as follows: i) One (1) year of experience will be credited for every 30 semester credits leading to a baccalaureate degree or associate degree in any of the disciplines described in “1” above, or a related field, up to a maximum of four (4) years. ii) A master’s degree in any of the disciplines described in “1” above, or a related field, will be credited for one (1) year of acceptable experience. iii) A license as a Professional Engineer or Registered Architect issued pursuant to the New York State Education Law will be credited for four (4) years of acceptable experience.

CEO / Business Co-Founder (f/m/d) role at startup FAMILY FLOW

FAMILY FLOW

Saarbrücken / Homburg, Saarland, Germany | Remote | Fulltime | Digital Health (DiGA)

About Family Flow

Family Flow is a scientifically grounded, trauma-sensitive parenting app that helps parents with their own history of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) manage the moment between a trigger and their reaction to their child — building a personalized 'Flow Plan' (trigger → warning signs → pause → skill → parenting strategy) instead of another generic parenting app.

The opportunity

The concept is built on more than 20 years of clinical and scientific work on child maltreatment led by Prof. Dr. med. Eva Möhler, Chair of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry at Saarland University, alongside DFKI researchers Patrick Gebhard and Jan Alexandersson. The idea and clinical content are finalized — what's missing is the team and funding to build and launch the app. We are looking for a CEO / Business co-founder (fundraising, tech and operations) to turn a validated clinical concept into a real product.

Tasks

What you will own

Company build-up & fundraising

- Lead incorporation of Family Flow and raise the funding needed for app development (German, French and English versions).

- Own the path to the German DiGA directory (digital health app reimbursement) and the parallel free-market / B2C launch.

Product & delivery

- Translate the finalized clinical concept and psychotherapeutic material into a software roadmap, in partnership with a tech/development team or subcontractor (e.g. potential partnerships with Pioneo, Pfeffermind or Charamel).

- Own day-to-day operations, as the current interdisciplinary team (DFKI + Child and Adolescent Psychiatry) is part-time only.

Go-to-market

- Build the launch plan for Germany and France, then wider Europe, including social-media-led B2C acquisition alongside the DiGA pathway.

Requirements

What you bring

Core experience

- Fundraising experience (grants and/or investors) and comfort building a company from an academic/clinical concept.

- Hands-on operations and project management skills; willingness to work full-time (the current founding team is part-time).

Especially valuable

- Experience with the digital health / DiGA regulatory pathway in Germany.

- Software/product background, or strong ability to manage external development partners.

- Interest in child psychiatry, trauma-informed care or parenting technology.

Benefits

Why join Family Flow

- A clinically validated concept backed by 20+ years of research and a published evidence base, not an unproven idea.

- Direct partnership with a University Professor and Chair of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry at Saarland University.

- Address a problem estimated to cost society €20 billion in Germany alone (Deutsche Traumafolgekostenstudie), with a clear DiGA reimbursement path.

Family Flow welcomes co-founder candidates regardless of gender, age, ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, sexual identity, or any other characteristic. This is a search for the right partner to build the company with, not a conventional hire.

Saarbrücken / Homburg, Saarland, Germany | Remote | Fulltime | Digital Health (DiGA)

About Family Flow

Family Flow is a scientifically grounded, trauma-sensitive parenting app that helps parents with their own history of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) manage the moment between a trigger and their reaction to their child — building a personalized 'Flow Plan' (trigger → warning signs → pause → skill → parenting strategy) instead of another generic parenting app.

The opportunity

About us
The appliedAI Initiative elevates Europe’s industry to become shapers in the age of AI, creating a future that we desire to live in. Through our ecosystem of strong partners, comprehensive programs, services and solutions we advance companies holistically on their AI journey. We share a mindset of collaboration and openness with our ecosystem of leading companies and tech players. Our common goal is to strengthen the European landscape, jointly creating unique knowledge for applying trustworthy AI. We believe that AI Agents will be the dominant topic for AI in the near future and that appliedAI with its partner ecosystem will impact how this technology is being used in industry and beyond in Europe.
Your mission
In every industrial company there is a problem the engineers have stopped raising, because everyone agrees it cannot be solved. A design that takes three days to validate. A variant that has to be quoted before anyone has drawn it. Forty years of engineering knowledge sitting in files nobody can search. Those problems are our work, and this is the role that takes them on: the technical lead for AI across design, simulation and manufacturing, trusted by clients with the question nobody has answered yet.
Your tasks will include:
Setting the technical direction for our industrial AI portfolio across design, simulation and manufacturing, and deciding which approach a problem actually deserves
Taking engineering problems that arrive badly defined and turning them into something that can be solved
Carrying the specialist authority in client projects, making the calls that decide whether a prototype becomes a system people rely on
Shaping new engagements with engineering and R&D leaders, from the first workshop to the signed proposal
Leaving behind reference architectures, evaluation methods and accelerators that the whole practice can build on
Growing the depth of the engineers around you through coaching, standards and hands-on reviews
Your profile
Ten years or more in computational engineering across design, simulation and manufacturing, earned through a doctorate in a computational field, or through an equal weight of industrial work
You know how the chain holds together: how geometry and constraints are set, how a design is validated numerically, how it becomes something a factory can make, and what breaks at every handover
You choose the method a problem deserves - surrogate and reduced-order models, physics-informed and data-driven modelling, optimisation, generative geometry, agents - and you still get somewhere when there is almost nothing to learn from
You start from what the customer needs rather than from what happens to sit in their database, and you can hold that conversation with an engineering leader in German or English, on their shop floor as readily as on a call
Extensive experience getting software in production, with the habits that come with it: testing, CI/CD, observability, and being the person who gets called when it stops
AI systems you have put into operation and kept running, models and agents alike: evaluated, guarded, affordable at load, and honest about how they fail
The commercial instinct to see which technically beautiful answer a client will actually buy, most likely built as a founder, an early employee, or an intrapreneur who carried real risk
What we offer
A highly qualified and motivated team of ~90 people is on a journey to change the rapidly evolving European AI Landscape
Experience the best of both worlds with our hybrid work model: You can choose to work from our vibrant offices - either at the IPAI in Heilbronn or the House of Communication in Munich - while also enjoying the flexibility to work remotely a few days each week
Opportunity to shape a variety of projects and the development of new, original content based on the latest developments in AI and its adoption in businesses
An atmosphere that encourages to think and experiment in new ways with software, hardware, and processes

Sports membership with Wellpass to access thousands of sports facilities all over Germany (and beyond), as well as online courses

College Aide

The New York County District Attorney's Office (DANY) has an immediate opening for a Part-Time College Aide in its Special Victim Division. Reporting directly to the Deputy Division Chief for Gender-Based Violence Policy. In this position the person will be responsible for supporting the Division in the development and implementation of policy, training, and external engagement projects and initiatives. Responsibilities include but are not limited to: • Assist the Deputy Chief in the coordination and administration of the SVD Advisory Council, the SVD Survivor Network, the Manhattan Sexual Assault Task Force, and other convenings and forums through which SVD engages with survivors, service providers and community members. • Assist the Deputy Chief in the coordination and administration of DANY’s Early Engagement Team Initiative and DANY’s partnership with the Clinical Forensic Fellowship Program and other tasks related to the recruitment and use of gender-based violence trial experts. • Assist the Deputy Chief in the coordination and implementation of SVD and officewide trainings. • Conduct state, local and federal research on SVD related legislation and policy and prepare reports for SVD and DANY’s policy team. • Support the Division’s partnership with the Community Partnerships Unit on SVD related community-based events and trainings. Preferred Requirements/Skills: • Excellent written and interpersonal communication skills, including community and external relations. • Exceptional organizational skills and strong attention to detail. • Ability to engage with the public in a professional manner, exercise sound judgment. • Ability to adapt to a fast-paced, deadline-oriented environment. • Strong online research skills and computer skills • Ability to work productively, independently, and collaboratively. • Ability to multi-task and meet deadlines. How to Apply: • Apply with a Cover Letter and Resume. Hours/Shift: • Monday-Friday between 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM, up to 20 hours per week. Additional Information: • Current office employees: To be eligible for a transfer or promotion, staff must have already served at least one (1) year in their current position and be in good standing. In addition, must meet the minimum qualifications of the position. • Looking for candidates that could commit to one (1) year to the hiring unit. • Authorization to work in the United States is required for this position.

For Assignment Level I: Matriculation at an accredited college or graduate school. Employment is conditioned upon continuance as a student in a college or graduate school. For Assignment Level II (Information Technology): Matriculation at an accredited college or graduate school. Employment is conditioned upon continuance as a student in a college or graduate school with a specific course of study in information technology, computer science, management information systems, data processing, or closely related field, including or supplemented by 9 semester credits in an acceptable course of study. For Assignment Level III (Information Technology Fellow): Matriculation at an accredited college or graduate school. Employment is conditioned upon continuance as a student in a college or graduate school with a specific course of study in information technology, computer science, management information systems, data processing, or other area relevant to the information technology project(s) assigned, including or supplemented by 9 semester credits in an acceptable course of study. Appointments to this Assignment Level will be made by the Technology Steering Committee through the Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications. SPECIAL NOTE Maximum tenure for all Assignment Levels in the title of College Aide is 6 years. How to Apply: • Apply with a Cover Letter and Resume. Hours/Shift: • Monday-Friday between 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM, up to 20 hours per week. Additional Information: • Current office employees: To be eligible for a transfer or promotion, staff must have already served at least one (1) year in their current position and be in good standing. In addition, must meet the minimum qualifications of the position. • Looking for candidates that could commit to one (1) year to the hiring unit. • Authorization to work in the United States is required for this position.

For Assignment Level I: Matriculation at an accredited college or graduate school. Employment is conditioned upon continuance as a student in a college or graduate school. For Assignment Level II (Information Technology): Matriculation at an accredited college or graduate school. Employment is conditioned upon continuance as a student in a college or graduate school with a specific course of study in information technology, computer science, management information systems, data processing, or closely related field, including or supplemented by 9 semester credits in an acceptable course of study. For Assignment Level III (Information Technology Fellow): Matriculation at an accredited college or graduate school. Employment is conditioned upon continuance as a student in a college or graduate school with a specific course of study in information technology, computer science, management information systems, data processing, or other area relevant to the information technology project(s) assigned, including or supplemented by 9 semester credits in an acceptable course of study. Appointments to this Assignment Level will be made by the Technology Steering Committee through the Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications. Community Assistant

The NYC Department of Probation (DOP) is a world leader in working creatively and effectively engaging with people under court-mandated community supervision. Through innovative partnerships with people and organizations throughout the New York City, DOP provides opportunities for those on probation to access services and opportunities that positively impact their life trajectory. Following the best current data on “what works,” staff at DOP engage in meaningful relationships with those on probation to enhance community safety and decrease recidivism. The Department of Probation is seeking to hire (6) six Community Assistants to support the day-to-day operations of the Department, enhances communication between DOP, City agencies, and the public, and assists probation clients and their families by providing information, referrals, and administrative support. Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following: - Perform routine clerical tasks including creating, sorting, filing, scanning, locating, and routing records, case files, and related materials - Process incoming cases for various levels of probation using logging and control systems for tracking and statistical purposes - Prepare case folders (both physical and electronic within the case management system) and assign cases to Probation Officers - Document court actions and case outcomes accurately in the case management system - Digitally photograph probation clients and maintain associated records - Provide front desk coverage on a rotating schedule by greeting probation clients, family members, and the public in a professional and courteous manner - Other duties as assigned.

1. There are no formal education or experience requirements for this position. However, the ability to understand and carry out simple instructions is required. 2. Candidates must be able to understand and be understood in English.

We are seeking a (Senior) People & Culture Specialist (f/m/d) to play a central role in building and scaling our People & Culture function as we grow. This role is instrumental in managing payroll, contracts, mobility, compliance, and reporting, while also acting as a trusted partner to our leadership team. You will be responsible for ensuring operational excellence across core HR processes, building reliable and scalable People Operations systems, supporting employees and managers in a fast-moving, international environment, and reducing dependency on manual workflows as the company scales.
The successful candidate will bring a blend of operational expertise, strategic partnership, process-building capabilities, and a people-centered approach to help us scale smoothly and sustainably.
To join our team, you should be excited to:
Scale People Operations and Global Mobility to support rapid company growth.
Take ownership of payroll for NL and DE, while supporting cases involving international payroll.
Manage contract management, employee lifecycle processes, compliance, and employee administration within our HRIS.
Build reliable, scalable systems and reduce dependency on manual workflows for daily People Operations.
Stabilize and document core People Operations and Global Mobility processes, including developing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
Deliver reporting and analytics that inform decision-making, translate People data into meaningful insights, and shape company policies.
Partner with external experts (legal, insurance, accounting, relocation/visa specialists, payroll providers) to ensure smooth operations as the company scales.
Build strong collaboration with other People & Culture areas, including Talent Acquisition, People Experience, and People Development.
Provide business support to the leadership team, acting as a sparring partner on People Operations and business partnering topics.
Contribute to writing and rolling out policies that support compliance, clarity, and culture.
Your Qualifications
At least 5-8 years of hands-on experience in People Operations within an international company, ideally in a scaling technology, engineering, or deep-tech environment.
Practical experience applying German labour law in an HR environment, with the ability to make informed day-to-day decisions.
Strong knowledge of HRIS systems (Personio required), payroll and benefits administration systems, and reporting analytics.
Experience managing immigration, visas, relocation, and international mobility programs is a plus.
Experience building processes, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and HR infrastructure.
Skilled in decision-making, collaboration, and stakeholder management, with proven ability to balance operational needs with employee experience.
Strong hands-on mindset with high attention to detail and the ability to execute in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to build trust and act with professionalism and integrity.
Fluency in German (minimum C1) and English.
Advanced Microsoft 365 skills.
Previous experience in a fast-growing startup environment, ideally in deep tech.

Fuel Cycle Fuel Recycling Lead (f/m/d)

About Focused Energy
Focused Energy is building the future of clean energy through laser-driven inertial fusion. Backed by our $240M Series A - the largest fully secured Series A in the global fusion industry we are scaling rapidly across multiple geographies.
Based in Germany and the US, we have brought together the top scientific and engineering minds using proven technologies to unlock fusion power at commercial scale. Focused Energy is working to realize game-changing scientific innovation that promises to deliver a clean, sustainable and abundant source of power globally.
Your Role
As a Fuel Cycle Fuel Recycling system lead, you will be responsible for guiding the design of tritium extraction from the chamber, breeding blanket, and wall, from early concept development through detailed design, licensing, and handover to construction and commissioning. The role combines deep technical expertise with organizational leadership to ensure technical excellence and effective cross-functional coordination throughout the project lifecycle.
What You'll Do
End-to-end accountability for the Fuel Cycle Fuel Recycling design.
Technical Leadership.
Define and govern the overall Fuel Cycle Fuel Recycling architecture, including configuration, major design parameters, and fundamental safety approach.
Resolve complex, cross-cutting technical issues that cannot be resolved at the engineer or discipline level.
Write key engineering deliverables including system design descriptions, design basis documents, interface control documents, and safety analysis inputs.
Lead a multidisciplinary team.
Report design status, risks, and issues clearly and regularly to the Fuel Cycle Group Leader.
Manage design change control processes to maintain schedule and cost discipline while preserving design integrity.
Who You Are
M.Sc. in nuclear engineering or chemical engineering.
Experience in fluid engineering.
Advanced experience specifically in process engineering simulation tools.
Minimum of 5 years of experience and 2 years of experience leading multidisciplinary technical teams.
Deep knowledge of process engineering for plant systems, safety analysis principles, and design basis development.
Experience designing and calculating fluid process
Knowledge of nuclear reactor physics.
Advanced fission reactor knowledge is an advantage.
Fusion is an advantage.
Mastery of process engineering tools.
Understanding processes, mechanical analysis and I&C.
Manage requirements, FMEA, licensing, documentation and control.
Project scheduling.

Nice-to-haves
Experience in fluid engineering applied to the nuclear industry.
Experience in advanced nuclear reactor systems.
Experience in advanced fusion systems.
Programming skills.
What We Offer
Innovative Technology & Mission: Be part of a cutting-edge company working on groundbreaking research in clean energy and scientific discovery.
Career Development: We invest in our people. This is an opportunity to join an early, growing company at the forefront of new technology, where you’ll have the opportunity to develop and grow your career.
Collaborative Culture: Work with great people in a dynamic, international environment with top-tier scientists, engineers and professionals passionate about solving global challenges.
Ownership: Take ownership from day 1 and drive impact by making decisions, solving challenges and shaping the future of our company.
Your Success is our Success: We offer a competitive salary and company ownership in the form of stock options, giving you a direct stake in our success and ownership in what we build together.
Vacation Days: We support your work-life-balance by granting you 30 days of vacation per year.
Snacks and Drinks: Our office fridges are never empty. Enjoy our healthy snacks and drinks. Our Darmstadt office even offers a canteen with delicious lunch options daily.
Retirement Plan: If you decide for a private pension plan, we will finance 20% on top of your monthly contributions, plus loyalty incentives.
Equipment: We offer state-of-the-art Windows or Apple Laptops. In addition, you will receive a keyboard, mouse and headset so you are fully equipped from day 1.
Events: We organize regular events to foster team bonding, encourage collaboration, and build a strong, supportive company culture. Connect with colleagues across departments, share ideas, and have fun together, both in and outside of the workplace.
Mobility with NAVIT: We partner with NAVIT to support your flexible commuting needs—whether it’s a public transportation ticket, taxi rides or car-sharing you choose what fits your lifestyle.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status.
Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Focused Energy will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

full_posting_text:
Fullstack Platform Engineer

WePush is a creator marketplace connecting brands with creators at scale. We’re looking for an experienced Fullstack Platform Engineer who enjoys architecture, infrastructure, and running real systems in production end-to-end.

This is a hands-on startup role, not a narrow DevOps position. You’ll build backend features, improve our infrastructure, and own what you ship from design to production.

Tasks

What you’ll do

Build backend services and APIs for campaigns, creator matching, marketplace operations, and payments.

Design clear domain models, database schemas, and service boundaries.

Build reliable background jobs that handle concurrency, retries, and failures correctly.

Contribute to our Web, Android, and iOS frontend when features require end-to-end ownership.

Improve deployments, CI/CD, monitoring, alerting, backups, and recovery.

Debug issues across application code, databases, infrastructure, and third-party APIs.

Make pragmatic architectural decisions while continuing to ship quickly.

Use AI coding agents as a core part of your daily development workflow.

Requirements

What we’re looking for:

Strong backend engineering experience in production environments.

Excellent knowledge of SQL, relational databases, transactions, locking, and data modelling.

Experience with Docker, Linux, cloud infrastructure, and CI/CD.

A good understanding of queues, scheduled jobs, APIs, networking, security, and observability.

Confidence reasoning about concurrency, idempotency, partial failures, and recovery.

Strong debugging skills across the full system.

Startup experience or a strong bias toward ownership and execution.

Good product judgment and an instinct for avoiding unnecessary complexity.

Experience using AI coding agents to plan, implement, test, review, and document software.

The ability to critically review, iterate on, and improve AI-generated code until it is high-quality and production-ready.

Our stack includes TypeScript, Node.js, React, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Docker, Linux, and Hack. Experience with every technology is not required, we care more about strong fundamentals and the ability to learn.

AI-native engineering:

Using AI agents is a requirement for this role, not an optional productivity tool.

We expect you to use them throughout the development process: exploring unfamiliar code, planning changes, implementing features, writing tests, investigating failures, reviewing work, and maintaining documentation.

This does not mean accepting generated code without understanding it. You remain responsible for architecture, security, correctness, and production outcomes. We are looking for someone who knows how to give agents useful context, break work into verifiable steps, review their output critically, and use them to increase both speed and quality.

You’ll probably enjoy this role if:

You have worked in an early stage startup/scale-up

You like owning systems after they go live.

You naturally ask what happens when a process crashes halfway through.

You can move between backend code, SQL, infrastructure, and debugging.

You prefer simple, dependable systems over fashionable architecture.

You are excited about developing with AI agents and actively improving how you use them.

Benefits

This is a rare opportunity to build at the intersection of AI, creator technology, and consumer products.

WePush is backed by experienced operators from companies including Spotify, Google and many more. We’re entering our next phase of growth with the ambition, speed, and ownership of a startup, but with a proven product and strong market traction.

As an AI Product Engineer, you won’t be sitting on the sidelines. You’ll work closely with the founders and product team to turn new AI capabilities into products used by brands and creators at scale.

What we offer:

Competitive salary and meaningful equity package

High ownership from day one with the freedom to ship, experiment, and influence product direction

Direct access to founders and leadership with fast decisions and minimal bureaucracy

A team of builders: Ambitious, pragmatic, and obsessed with moving fast

An in-person culture in our Berlin office, with flexibility for home office days

Public transport pass, gym membership, recurring team lunches, and other perks

A front-row seat to building a category-defining technology company

Regardless of who you are, where you come from, how you look, or what music is playing in your headphones, you are welcome.

If you are a builder and move fast, this role is for you.

DCAS's mission is to make city government work for all New Yorkers. From managing New York City’s most iconic courthouses and municipal buildings, to purchasing over $1 billion annually in goods and services for more than 80 City agencies — what we do ensures that all agencies can deliver on their mission. Our reach touches every facet of city government and is instrumental to the successful day-to-day operations of the City of New York. Our commitment to equity, effectiveness, and sustainability guides our work providing City agencies with the critical resources and support needed to succeed, including: • Recruiting, hiring, and training City employees. • Managing 56 public buildings. • Acquiring, selling, and leasing City property. • Purchasing over $1 billion in goods and services for City agencies. • Overseeing the greenest municipal vehicle fleet in the country. • Leading the City's efforts to reduce carbon emissions from government operations. When you work at DCAS, you're not just working for one agency, but in service of them all. It's an opportunity to provide impactful support, quality customer service, and help protect the future of New York City for generations to come. Visit our website at nyc.gov/dcas to learn more about the work we do. Facilities Management & Construction (FMC) manages, operates, and maintains 56 City-owned buildings throughout the five boroughs, working to provide clean, safe, and energy efficient space for the tenants in these public buildings. FMC is dedicated to both the daily maintenance of the public buildings, managed by Building Services, Fire & Life Safety, and other critical field staff, as well as to long-term renovation and rehabilitation projects, which are managed by a dedicated staff of architects, engineers, and other professional technical experts. FMC also oversees the daily operations of all elevators across the DCAS public buildings portfolio. Construction & Technical Services (CTS) under FMC consists of a design, construction and technical team of architects, engineers, elevator mechanics, as well as project & property managers who provide services for time-sensitive rehabilitation, renovations, and maintenance in City-owned properties. Its design team performs in-house designs, conducts field inspections, and ensures design compliance with Local Laws. This team also performs reviews of design consultant drawings to assure accountability for the needed renovations. The construction team manages and oversees time-sensitive construction projects to ensure daily activities comply with contract drawings, specifications, building codes, budget, and timelines. This team assesses field conditions, prepares reports, and coordinates meetings with contractors, consultants, and the in-house design crew to address variations from the original design drawings to accommodate field conditions and/or client requests. The technical team manages the maintenance and surplus in City-Owned properties, handles the contracts for services including, but not limited to, interior rehabilitation and construction, waterfront construction, sidewalk repair, fencing, demolition, pest control, erection of scaffolding; handles and maintains the design and management of site safety projects (Local Laws and Violations) and maintains and repairs all elevators, escalators and ADA lifts throughout City-Owned buildings within the five boroughs. The DCAS Trade Shops help with all in-house construction and repair services needed within DCAS-managed sites. The Shops perform small-scale renovations such as partitions/drywall work, rough and finish carpentry, interior/exterior painting, electrical and plumbing repairs, structural steel, concrete, and masonry work and manufacture in-house replacement of parts for obsolete equipment and locksmith services and Mayoral Ceremonies and Special Events. Under the direct supervision of the Chief Architect, the employee’s duties and responsibilities will be, but will not be limited to the following: •Assist inhouse technical staff with design details before and during construction. •Assist inhouse technical staff with the management and coordination of construction projects. •Assisting inhouse staff to review design drawings according to field conditions and help prepare sketches for omitted conditions found within the designs. •Assist in the review of construction/consultants reports to help determine payment progress. •Assist inhouse staff to conduct field inspections for a fair and reasonable standard of proposed negotiations, based on field conditions. •Assist inhouse staff in developing change order negotiations, based on technical bulletins, drawings, and sketches, and reviewing the validity of extra work costs and credits of the work performed is not part of the original contract. •Assist inhouse staff with the review of all change orders submitted for DCAS in-house projects; its validity, cost before its submission to Engineering Audit. •Assist inhouse staff with the review of construction requisitions based on work progress is in conformance to the plans and specifications reports and determine final payment amounts. •Assist inhouse staff with the preparation of project estimates based on building needs (Capital/Expense New Needs) and as proposed by the in-house staff. •Assist inhouse staff in the review of construction projects estimates for DCAS facilities as submitted by other agencies and reviewing consultants and contractors estimates for accuracy and completeness. •Assist inhouse staff in the review of contract documents comprised of drawings and specifications to attain estimates of value(s). •Assisting in-house staff in the pricing and the forecasting of cost trends and factors. To Apply: Please go to www.nyc.gov/careers and search for Job ID # 797797. For current City employees please go to www.nyc.gov/ess and log into Employee Self Service. NO PHONE CALLS, FAXES OR PERSONAL INQUIRIES PERMITTED. NOTE: ONLY THOSE CANDIDATES UNDER CONSIDERATION WILL BE CONTACTED.

For Assignment Level III (Information Technology Fellow): Matriculation at an accredited college or graduate school. Product Growth Manager

We're looking for an ambitious PM ready to build Nelly's Growth function from scratch - owning the full journey from sign-up to habit across our software, AI, and fintech surfaces, with direct impact on NRR. If you want real ownership and zero hand-holding, this is it.

About Nelly
We are building the AI-Driven Financial Operating System for European healthcare, solving the biggest challenges for patients and practices. We create what no bank or software platform can handle. Our all-in-one platform transforms chaotic administrative processes into intelligent, automated workflows, from patient care to billing to next-generation payments. Because we truly believe: healthcare should be less about paperwork and more about people.
Why?
Because Europe is facing a massive shortage of medical professionals. And if we don't rethink the way practices work, the system won't be able to keep up. With our Series B funding of over €50 million from world-class investors, we are turning our vision into reality.
What sets us apart:
We work with the best team, which is why we give everything together every day. We believe in Talent Density, because exceptional people make everyone around them better. At Nelly, we move fast and expect everyone to keep up. Stagnation isn’t an option, which is why we invest heavily in growth. AI isn't a nice-to-have at Nelly. We expect you to use it every day and give you everything you need to do so. You get trust and ownership and we expect you to speak up, even when it's uncomfortable.
Joining us, you will:
Translate Nelly's company vision into specific, prioritized bets across acquisition, activation, and monetisation, informed by data, experimentation, and customer behavior
Own the end-to-end user journey: from partial sign-up through setup, first value, and habit formation - across Nelly's software, AI, and fintech products, and continuously sharpen each stage
Build platform-level growth capabilities that compound across surfaces , not features that live in one place
Design and run a rigorous experimentation and measurement program. Form hypotheses, define metrics, ship A/B tests at high velocity, learn fast, and ship what moves the numbers
Collaborate deeply with Design, Engineering, Marketing, and Product Leadership on both strategy and execution
Inform pricing, packaging, and self-serve strategy in partnership with GTM and finance leadership - including how we package across software, AI, and fintech to drive expansion (vertical & geo)
What you'll bring:
Note: If you don't meet all the criteria, we still encourage you to apply and make the case for why you'd be a great fit. If you're exceptional talent, we're happy to adapt.
Shipped exceptional B2B/prosumer growth products in high-velocity environments - you care deeply about user outcomes and winning with the product
3+ years in product management with hands-on PLG (and ideally PLS) experience: you've built and owned elaborated growth motions on complex B2B workflow products
High agency and high learning velocity: you run a high volume of hypothesis-driven bets, move fast in ambiguity, say "no" when needed, and are comfortable building from zero
Strong analytical skills and data mindset around A/B testing, optimization, and defining growth metrics
Strong data mindset: you create data acquisition and evaluation strategies, track product and agent metrics (utilization rates, precision & recall), understand online vs. offline eval trade-offs, and use insights to drive better customer outcomes
Passion for AI technology and its potential to reshape product-led growth
Excellent cross-functional collaboration across Engineering, Design, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success
Even better if you have:
German or Italian proficiency - you can discuss real work with dentists, ZFAs/ZMVs, and billing partners
Experience growing products for SMB customers in less-digital European verticals (healthcare, construction, legal, architecture, or similar) where adoption is hard-won and not a given
Experience with self-serve, freemium, or PQL-driven growth motions
Experience with high-growth SaaS products using usage or outcome-based pricing, where you owned strategies to drive net revenue retention (NRR) growth
What we offer:
Deutschlandticket (public transport pass covering all of Germany) or a Swapfiets membership to cruise through the city
Urban Sports membership to sweat, stretch, or sauna your way through the week
Top of the line working equipment
Flexible hours and a hybrid setup in the heart of Berlin
Enjoy up to 4 weeks of workation wherever inspiration hits
A cozy, dog-friendly office where good vibes are basically mandatory
A fridge full of cold drinks and snacks waiting to be claimed
We welcome applications from people of all genders and backgrounds, regardless of origin or age. If you're convinced you're the right fit for this role - even if your CV doesn't match the requirements 100% - tell us why.

Contract Administrator

Applicants must be permanent in the Procurement Analyst civil service title to apply. The New York City Employees’ Retirement System seeks a Procurement Analyst in the Procurement unit within the Legal Division. Under general supervision, with latitude for independent initiative and decision making, performs work of moderate difficulty in purchasing goods, services and/or construction, and in processing procurement documents and contracts. Duties will include but are not limited to: Key Responsibilities • Prepare, review, and evaluate solicitation documents to ensure conformity to agency requirements and citywide standards and work with the program end users to develop solicitation requirements • Prepare Pre- Solution Pre-Solicitation review, Recommendation for Award, Reasonable Price and Responsibility Determinations and other documentation required by the NYC to support the procurement and contract award process • Oversee and manage pre-solicitation review activities • Research and identify goods required to be obtained through the Preferred Source method • Solicit bids via various Procurement Methods such as NYC Requirement Contracts, GSA, OGS, MWBE Small Purchase, Small Purchase, Negotiated Acquisition, Sole Source, Request for Bids, and Request for Proposals • Examine bid samples to determine compliance with specifications or bid standards • Make determinations for the most reasonable price in relation to market conditions • Make recommendations for small purchase awards, modifications, emergency purchases and extensions of time to contracts • Consult with and advise program personnel on issues relating to procurement actions • Analyze vendors past performance, financial status, and other factors to determine vendor responsibility • Participate in the implementation of procedures for procurement activities • Ensure compliance with the requirements for program evaluations of vendor performance • Utilize software application, in addition to electronic and online databases to monitor procurement processing • Ensure compliance with Federal, State, & NYC local regulations • Carry out all procurement activities in full compliance with NYC PPB Rules and Laws and in accordance with procedures established • Conduct open market research • Collaborate with vendors, programs, fiscal staff, and oversight agencies to address any procurement related issues to ensure prompt payment • Perform special projects and related work as required

1. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college and six months of satisfactory full-time professional experience in procurement of goods, services, construction or construction-related services, or professional, technical or administrative experience in contract negotiation/management; or 2. An associate degree or completion of 60 semester credits from an accredited college, and 18 months of satisfactory, full-time professional experience as described in “1” above; or 3. A four-year high school diploma or its educational equivalent and two and one-half years of satisfactory full time professional experience as described in “1” above; or 4. A combination of education and/or experience equivalent to “1”, “2”, or “3” above. College education may be substituted for professional experience under “2” or “3” above at the rate of 30 semester credits from an accredited college for 6 months of experience. However, all candidates must have at least a four year high school diploma or its educational equivalent and 6 months of the experience described in “1” above. SPECIAL NOTES: To be eligible for placement in Assignment Level II, individuals must have, after meeting the minimum requirements, either one year served at Assignment Level I or one additional year of the experience described in "1" above. To be eligible for placement in Assignment Level III, individuals must have, after meeting the minimum requirements, either one year served at Assignment Level II or two additional years of the experience described in "1" above, at least one year of which must have been supervisory, or spent performing professional procurement duties equivalent to those performed at Assignment Level III.

• Ability to demonstrate knowledge of procurement lifecycle from requisition through contract close-out across all procurement methodologies • Excellent written and verbal communications skills • Effective problem-solving skills, and the ability to prioritize, manage time, and engage in multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment • Excellent analytical, interpersonal, and organizational skills • Excellent attention to detail and organization • Ability to recognize and adjust to change • Collaborative nature while remaining action-oriented • Must have an in-depth knowledge of the City’s procurement policies and rules as well as knowledge of federal and state grant procurement requirements. • Experience collaborating with internal stakeholders • NYC Certified procurement professional

responsibilities_text:
As a Founder’s Associate, you will work closely with the Founder and CEO and leadership team to help drive the company’s strategic priorities and operational execution.
In this role, you will take ownership of high-impact, cross-functional projects across the business. These may range from supporting strategic initiatives in commercial, product, and operations teams to improving internal processes, building organisational structures, and helping ensure alignment as the company scales.
This role is ideal for someone who is excited by our mission of enabling anyone to invest in capital markets. You will be close to many strategic initiatives and interact beyond lemon.markets towards our parent company, dwpbank. You will get the best of both worlds: the opportunity to work closely with experienced experts across functions while taking on meaningful ownership in a dynamic and ambitious environment.
This is going to be the ride of a lifetime for someone, who thrives in a fast-moving environment, enjoys solving ambiguous problems, and wants to gain first-hand experience in how a high-growth fintech infrastructure company is built.
You will:
Support the Founder and CEO on strategic and operational projects that drive company goals and priorities.
Own and lead projects with a deep focus on brokerage, custody and capital markets, this is where you will spend a significant part of your time and where domain knowledge is essential.
Analyse market developments, competitor dynamics, and trends across the European brokerage, wealth, and investment infrastructure landscape.
Take ownership of special projects that support the next stage of lemon.markets’ growth.
Lead and mentor the Founder’s Associate Intern team, providing structure, guidance, and prioritisation across projects while helping develop their skills and ensuring high-quality execution.
Contribute to refining and scaling internal processes, documentation, and operating structures across the company, especially in light of what becomes possible with AI.
Help develop, structure, and execute cross-functional initiatives across teams.
Act as a connector across the organisation by understanding team priorities, spotting gaps and blockers early, and helping drive effective cross-functional collaboration.
You’ll be successful in this role if you:

full_posting_text:
Chief Operations Officer/Deputy Commissioner of Ferries

Serves as the Chief Operations Officer of the Staten Island Ferry and Deputy Commissioner of the Ferry Division for the New York City Department of Transportation. Provides executive leadership and direction for the safe and efficient operation and maintenance of the vessels, terminals and facilities of the Staten Island Ferry, including management of over 600 employees, including 450 mariners, and an annual expense budget $63 million (PS), $44 million (OTPS) and 10 Year Capital Plan of approximately $450 million. In collaboration with the Commissioner and First Deputy Commissioner, serves as a member of top management providing commitment, leadership, and the highest levels of management to the Staten Island Ferry's Safety Management System (SMS), in accordance with International Safety Management (ISM) Code requirements. Regulates private ferry operations within the City of New York. EXAMPLES OF TYPICAL TASKS: Responsible to serve as the highest level of authority with the SMS in matters relating to administration, engineering, operations and safety. Be available and respond 24/7 to issues and emergencies. Establish and coordinate the effective implementation of a Safety & Environmental Protection Policy. Oversee activities of senior management of functional areas, including customer relations and customer service. Ensure the entire Staten Island Ferry system is operated safely and effectively in accordance with principles of good seamanship and all applicable laws and regulations, including U.S. Coast Guard regulations. Responsible for ensuring that all Staten Island Ferry personnel are properly trained and fully familiar with all applicable regulations, including NYCDOT policies and regulations. Plan and execute new technology for the ferry including replacement vessels. Represent the agency to and interacts with other local, state and federal government agencies, elected officials, private ferry operators, city unions and other stakeholders. Performs related managerial duties. The Staten Island Ferry is a critical link in the City's transportation infrastructure and carries over 17 million passengers annually between the St. George Terminal in Staten Island and the Whitehall Terminal in Lower Manhattan, operating 365 days per year around the clock. The Ferry Division exemplifies DOT's mission in providing for the safe, efficient, equitable and environmentally responsible movement of people and goods in the City of New York.

1. Baccalaureate or higher degree in operations management, business management, marine transportation, nautical science, marine engineering, or related discipline from an accredited college. Maritime industry relevant work experience may be substituted for degree.

1. Possession of a valid Merchant Mariner Credential (MMC) issued by the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG), with endorsement as Master (unlimited tonnage) or Chief Engineer (unlimited propulsion power) strongly preferred. 2. Strong background in all aspects of maritime management, including operations, engineering, maintenance and repair, personnel management and regulation issues. 3. Experience with implementation and/or operation of Safety Management Systems in accordance with ISM code. 4. Superb managerial and communication skills. 5. Experience with passenger ferry systems in a managerial capacity is preferred, but not required.

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. Where exactly does probabilistic end and deterministic begin?

What success looks like
6 months:
Architecture decided. One real use case from the core business runs in production and is used daily. Your first engineers are hired.
12 months:
Several agentic use cases in regular operation. The control layer holds up in a real review, and evaluation runs against closed cases, not test data.
24 months:
Automation is a capability of the organization, not of individuals. Every acquired firm runs on the same base, and your team ships without you in the room.
Where it leads:
the full CTO mandate – a management career earned by contribution, not by years served.
What you bring
You have built something that ran in production and was used by people who did not build it – as founding engineer, engineering lead, technical co-founder or in a comparable role.
You have taken agentic systems into production and know where they break.
You have integrated against systems that fight back: legacy ERPs, banking backends, badly documented interfaces.
You write production code. AI is your everyday tool, and your position on the stack comes from what you built and threw away.
You work in German, because our clients and tax advisors do, and you build in person in Munich.
You learn from practitioners, and you set the highest standard in everything you ship – not because someone checks, but because mediocrity bothers you.
A plus, not a requirement
A regulated field where mistakes have consequences: fintech, banking tech, payments (N26, Trade Republic, Solaris, Klarna, Mollie, Pleo) or software for professional services (Personio, Workato).
Knowledge of accounting, tax or DATEV.

Building, not managing.

An operating company, not a software vendor.

In person in Munich, not a distributed team.
An architecture being decided and a team finding its standards need a shared room.

Turn our data into the edge.

Every firm that joins Vogel runs on what you build – one decision of yours reaches several thousand clients from day one, and more with every acquisition.

Substance behind you.
A profitable, growing business – no funding round decides whether your team exists.
FAQ
1. Was ist Vogel – und wo arbeitet ihr?
Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands – seit 1959, inhabergeführt in zweiter Generation, mit eigenem Kapital – und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir arbeiten an drei Standorten: Aalen als gewachsenem Stammsitz, Bopfingen im Kerngeschäft und München als neuem Hub. An allen dreien suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen – von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den Teams, die das Fundament darunter bauen.
2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?
Bewusst breit – und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen, bevor du dich bewirbst. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala – zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen. Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.
3. Wie viel – und wie – wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?
Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen und sehen uns im Normalfall täglich im Büro – Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.
4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?
Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. In der Regel sind es vier Schritte: eine schriftliche Aufgabe, in der du zu acht Fragen Position beziehst – KI ist ausdrücklich erlaubt, wir bitten nur um eine kurze Selbstauskunft dazu; ein Gespräch von einer halben Stunde; eine gemeinsame Arbeitssitzung an einem echten Problem aus unserem Alltag; und ein Termin vor Ort mit dem Team und gemeinsamem Essen. Wie viele Schritte es tatsächlich werden, hängt von der Rolle ab: Bei Praktikum und Werkstudium fällt der Vor-Ort-Termin weg, für Schülerjobs genügt ein Gespräch, bei Senior-Rollen kommt ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsnachmittag dazu. Vorab kannst du einen Zehn-Minuten-Call buchen, in dem nur du fragst. In der Regel hörst du nach jedem Schritt innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns.
5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?
Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung – du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test – liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft anhand von sechs Kriterien: Impact, Judgement, Communication, Execution, Growth und Values.
6. Wie entwickle ich mich – welche Karrierewege gibt es?
Zwei aktive Wege: die IC-Karriere (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) über die Stufen Expert, Senior, Lead und Principal – und die Management-Karriere (Führung, Personalverantwortung) über Manager, Senior Manager, Director und VP. Beide werden gleich vergütet, und beide müssen nicht nach oben führen: Wer auf einer Stufe bleibt und dort weiter in die Tiefe geht, ist bei uns genauso richtig. Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke – vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.
7. Team, Kultur, Urlaub?
Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. Dazu Social Events und Offsites in regelmäßigem Rhythmus – nicht als Pflichtprogramm, sondern weil ein gutes Team auch abseits der Arbeit Zeit teilt.
Benefits sind bei uns nicht das Sahnehäubchen, sondern das, was Intensität über Jahre tragbar macht: Examensförderung mit 25.000 EUR Qualifizierungsbudget und drei Monaten Freistellung, 100-prozentige Übernahme der Kinderbetreuung, EGYM Wellpass, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Job-Ticket mit 90 % Zuschuss, Homeoffice-Ausstattung und ein Gerät deiner Wahl aus unserem Katalog, ein Buch im Monat aus dem Vogel-Kanon – und KI-Tools ohne Token-Limit und ohne Budgetdeckel. Urlaub: 28 Tage.

The Department of Design & Construction, Safety & Site Support (SSS) Division seeks a Division Administrative Officer (DAO). The DAO is responsible for providing high-level administrative and operational support to Division leadership and staff, with primary responsibility for human resources, recruitment, workforce coordination, and administrative oversight. The successful candidate will lead and coordinate the Division’s recruitment and personnel activities and HR coordination, serve as the key resource to managers and staff on HR policies and procedures, and liaise with various divisions within the Agency. The successful candidate will be responsible to: monitor recruitment activity and routinely update Senior Leadership, maintain all related hiring communications with hiring and interview teams; schedule interviews and manage entire personnel onboarding process; prepare personnel action requests for Division head approval and submission to HR; update and maintain vacancy and personnel action requests log; coordinate and assist with hiring pools and various recruitment initiatives and events; liaise with Technology & Innovation, Operations and Facilities Management for Safety & Site Support staff placement and relocation, and oversee coordination of Division training and staff development needs. Additional duties will include providing high-level administrative support, including preparation and review of documents, correspondence, reports, presentations, and other materials; support Division operations by monitoring administrative processes, identifying issues and opportunities for improvement, and ensuring compliance with applicable agency policies, procedures, and requirements. Please note: All candidates must be currently authorized to work full-time in the United States (U.S.). In compliance with Public Law 99-603, candidates are required to present original documents proving citizenship or the legal right to work in the U.S. DDC is unable to support or sponsor any visa application or visa extension, including but not limited to OPT/STEM visas, H-1B visas, F-1 practical training, permanent residence sponsorship, or any proposed change of visa type. DDC does not offer a training program as required by U.S. immigration law and is not hiring temporary employees. Candidates must have proper work authorization when an employment offer is made. Additionally, educational credentials must be from a U.S. Department of Education-recognized accredited institution. Credentials from foreign institutions require independent equivalency verification from an approved evaluation service. A list of providers (fees apply) is available at: https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dcas/downloads/pdf/employment/nyc-dcas-foreign-education-evaluation-guide.pdf. All applicants, including City Employees: Please go to NYC Government Jobs Explore Careers City of New York, go to Search for Open Jobs, and type in the Job ID # listed above. OUTREACH SPECIALIST

The Department of Social Services (DSS) is comprised of the administrative units of the New York City Human Resources Administration (HRA) and the Department of Homeless Services (DHS). HRA is dedicated to fighting poverty and income inequality by providing New Yorkers in need with essential benefits such as Food Assistance and Emergency Rental Assistance. DHS is committed to preventing and addressing homelessness in New York City by employing a variety of innovative strategies to help families and individuals successfully exit shelter and return to self-sufficiency as quickly as possible. The NYC Public Engagement Unit (PEU) identifies and executes proactive strategies to connect New Yorkers to key City services. Relying heavily on data analytics, new technologies, and large-scale outreach tactics, the unit identifies New Yorkers in need of assistance and helps them navigate and obtain City services. The Public Engagement Unit consists of teams of specialists who are trained to effectively engage New Yorkers and connect them with vital resources. The Unit uses data to identify demographics that likely want or need city services; and works with partner agencies, elected officials, community groups, non-profit organizations, and service providers to engage directly with communities and subject matter experts in all five boroughs. The unit is frequently involved in citywide events, special projects in conjunction with multiple city agencies, and targeted days of action. PEU is seeking Outreach Specialists with experience with community-based outreach and/or case management. Successful candidates should have at least one year of community, issue, labor or political organizing experience, and excellent communications and outreach skills. The candidate should have demonstrated the ability to closely track metrics and outcomes and be detail-oriented and organized. Familiarity with New York City government, housing issues, and a commitment to helping others is preferred. The NYC Public Engagement Unit (PEU) is recruiting two (2) Community Associates to function as TSU Outreach Specialist who will: •Engage New Yorkers through various outreach tactics including door-to-door canvassing, phone calls, and peer-to-peer texting, to assess their needs and inform them of relevant City services and resources. •Provide ongoing case management to help New Yorkers access benefits, with a primary focus on housing benefits and services. •Conduct outreach Days of Action and other community events. •Respond to incoming calls from the Tenant Helpline. •Maintain ongoing reporting and communication with their assigned supervisor. •Liaise with community stakeholders, including community-based organizations and agency partners. •Support partners with outreach efforts to provide additional resources and information to New Yorkers citywide. •Assist with special projects, as needed. A successful candidate will know how to run an effective meeting, read the room, and build strong relationships with diverse groups of stakeholders. They will be able to synthesize input from staff with hard data to create viable outreach strategies. Hours/Shift: Monday – Friday 9am – 5pm or Tuesday - Saturday 10:30am – 6:30pm

Qualification Requirements 1. High school graduation or equivalent and three years of experience in community work or community centered activities in an area related to duties described above; or 2. Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1" above.

•1 year of experience with community, issues, labor, or political organizing. •Excellent interpersonal skills and a proven ability to engage people in conversation. •Strong written and oral communication skills in English; Spanish is a plus. •Ability to prioritize and effectively manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced work environment. •Willingness to learn, be flexible and adapt to work assignments in a variety of situations and problem solve.

The Public Engagement Unit consists of teams of specialists who are trained to effectively engage New Yorkers and connect them with vital resources. The Unit uses data to identify demographics that likely want or need city services; and works with partner agencies, elected officials, community groups, non-profit organizations, and service providers to engage directly with communities and subject matter experts in all five boroughs. GTM Internship

About Peec AI
Peec AI is the analytics platform for AI search. People increasingly discover products and make buying decisions through ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Google's AI Overviews instead of traditional search, and most brands have no idea where they show up in those answers. Peec gives marketing, SEO, and growth teams the data to see exactly that: how visible their brand is across AI platforms, how they compare to competitors, and where to win.
We are defining this category, and the market is moving with us. Peec is a Series A company backed by 20VC and Singular, past $15M ARR, with a 80+ person team across our Berlin HQ and our new New York office.
About the role
We’re looking for a GTM Intern to support our sales and revenue teams as we scale Peec AI’s global customer base. In this role, you’ll work closely with the sales team on deal execution, sales content, and CRM operations while helping improve the systems and automations that power our revenue engine. You’ll gain hands-on exposure to modern B2B SaaS sales, from outreach and pipeline management to revenue operations and automation, making this an ideal role for someone eager to learn quickly and contribute to a fast-growing startup’s go-to-market efforts.
What you’ll do
Support the sales team in closing deals and managing key client relationships
Develop sales content - from outreach sequences to pitch decks and case studies
Design and implement automations across our sales stack to improve efficiency and tracking
Contribute to revenue operations by analyzing metrics, improving CRM hygiene, and streamlining data flows
Jump into new challenges, learn fast, and help make things happen
What we’re looking for
Currently studying, on a gap semester, or recently graduated, and available immediately full-time for 3-6 months
Strong interest in B2B SaaS, startups, and revenue growth
Exceptional communication skills, written and verbal - you’re comfortable reaching out to people and building relationships
Analytical mindset and structured approach to problem-solving
Solid grasp of technology and excitement to work hands-on with cutting-edge AI and automation tools
Self-starter with a bias for action, eager to learn, and comfortable with ambiguity
Low-ego team player who’s easy to work with and doesn’t shy away from rolling up their sleeves for operational tasks
Available immediately
Bonus Points
Experience with tools like HubSpot, Clay, Lemlist, Apollo, Notion, or n8n
Exposure to sales operations, CRM management, or data-driven growth
Have built your own startup or cool projects you’re proud of
What we offer
A rolling internship program with flexible start dates (minimum 3-month duration)
A high-impact internship working directly with the founders at one of Europe’s fastest-growing Series A startups
Real ownership and visibility across the sales and revenue organization
Regular team events and off-sites
Paid Meal & Uber rides when working late
The most beautiful office space and work environment in Berlin
Compensation: €3K per month
